prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with whiplash after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 19 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1291; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: The patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with cervical whiplash. The mechanism and force of the collision fit well with the injury described. Over the course of nineteen visits, care followed a typical progression of manual therapy, guided range-of-motion exercises, and home stretching, with visit frequency gradually reduced as symptoms eased. Cervical examination showed reduced range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness that support the reported injury, while neurological screening, reflexes, and strength testing were within normal limits. The patient reports a remote, minor strain involving the same region several years ago, which resolved completely without lasting limitation. Billing records reflect single entries for each service with no duplicated charges. At discharge the patient was improving, with residual stiffness expected to resolve with continued self-directed exercise.
